name: ios-app
title: iOS app
summary: Screens that look right in light, in dark and with VoiceOver.

rules.text: Every screen has a light and a dark screenshot test.
rules.why: a screen that reads well in one mode can be unreadable in the other.

rules.text: No change removes a VoiceOver label from a screen.
rules.why: a missing label makes a control invisible to someone who cannot see the screen.

questions.ask: The oldest iOS it supports is

items.title: One command runs the app's tests on a simulator
items.criterion: scripts/test.sh builds the app, runs its tests on an iOS simulator for the oldest iOS it supports, and exits with an error when a test fails. Before this item the script does not exist, so the check fails.
items.brief:
Files:
- scripts/test.sh
Test:
- sh scripts/test.sh runs every test; sh scripts/test.sh <TestCase> runs one test case through xcodebuild -only-testing

items.title: Every screen has a light and a dark screenshot test
items.criterion: Each screen is drawn in light mode and in dark mode and compared with a recorded screenshot of each. The ScreenModeTests test case holds these tests and fails before the change.
items.brief:
Files:
- the app's test target
Test:
- ScreenModeTests draws each screen in both modes and compares it with its recorded screenshot

items.title: Every control keeps its VoiceOver label
items.criterion: Every control a person can tap on each screen has a VoiceOver label. The AccessibilityLabelTests test case checks each screen and fails before the change.
items.brief:
Files:
- the app's test target
Test:
- AccessibilityLabelTests opens each screen and fails on a tappable control without a label
